title: ADR-001: Adopt OpenTelemetry for Distributed Tracing
author: Marcus Rodriguez (Tech Lead)
context: Our transition from a monolith to microservices requires unified observability across services written in Go, TypeScript, and Python. Custom logging has led to blind spots during production incidents.
decision: We decided to adopt OpenTelemetry as the standard observability framework across all backend services. All new services must implement OTel tracing and export to our central Jaeger/Prometheus backend.

positive: Unified trace IDs across all service boundaries
negative: Initial migration effort for legacy services
Memory overhead of OTel collector sidecars

title: ADR-002: Vitess Sharding for High-Volume User Tables
author: Priya Patel (Backend Lead)
context: User tables have exceeded 450M rows, causing p99 query latency degradation on identity lookups. Single-instance PostgreSQL vertical scaling is nearing its hardware limit.
decision: We decided to implement hash-based sharding on user_id using Vitess as the distributed database proxy layer. The transition will begin with a non-production proof of concept followed by phased production cutover.

positive: Horizontal scalability to billions of records
Transparent SQL routing for application tier
negative: Operational complexity of managing Vitess clusters

title: ADR-003: Deprecate Legacy REST API v1 in Favor of v2 gRPC and REST
author: Sarah Chen (VP Engineering)
context: API v1 suffers from inconsistent response envelopes, unversioned schema mutations, and lack of rate limiting. Only 3% of active traffic originates from v1, but maintenance overhead remains significant.
decision: We decided to deprecate internal and external v1 API endpoints with an effective sunset date of December 1st, 2026. Deprecation notice and migration docs will be issued with mandatory 90-day lead time.

positive: Reduction of attack surface and code maintenance
Cost savings on legacy server fleets
negative: Requires coordinated migration with enterprise partners
Risk of breaking downstream third-party integrations

title: ADR-004: Standardize Frontend State Management on Zustand
author: Aisha Kumar (Frontend Lead)
context: Multiple frontend repositories currently utilize a fragmented set of state management libraries (Redux Toolkit, MobX, Context API), resulting in slow developer onboarding and code reuse barriers.
decision: Let's standardize on Zustand for all client-side global state management across web applications. Legacy Redux stores will be migrated incrementally during regular feature iterations.

negative: Learning curve for developers accustomed to Redux devtools action replay
